uncited: Custom Shading Models provide a mechanism for users to define arbitrary lighting computations per-voxel or per-hit-point, bypassing standard lookup tables or fixed-function pipelines.
This family solves the problem of applying non-standard, physically based, or highly stylized lighting effects to volume-rendered or ray-marched geometry.

It differs from sibling methods like [Phong Shading with SDF Normals](1977-phong-shading-with-sdf-normals.md) by allowing complete algorithmic freedom rather than restricting the user to a specific analytic model, and from [Distance Color Blending](791-distance-color-blending.md) by operating on lighting calculations rather than color accumulation.
The core mechanism for implementing custom shading in volume rendering, as defined by the VolPack API, involves replacing the default shading lookup shader with a user-defined callback.
